## Closing record — merged as `103729e90c` (Gerrit 1993, patchset 2)

Both ACs are met and ticked (box state only; AC prose untouched, verified byte-identical
before the edit):

- **AC 1 — identical fit.** `_JiraSanitizer.fit_comment` now returns exactly the marker-free
  text the Cloud send path lands, proven under BOTH `rich_text_cutover` settings.
- **AC 2 — a test drives both.** `diffing/test_comment_dedup_key_matches_send_fit.py` asserts
  the landed body equals the comparison key for an over-length comment, and was RED on the
  pre-fix code. It ended up STRONGER than the AC asked: the landed side is CAPTURED from a real
  `acli_cli_ops.add_comment` call rather than re-derived, so it also detects the send path
  drifting away again.

Patchset 1 earned both votes and was NOT submitted: a code-review advisory correctly identified
its oracle as a tautology, and seeding this ticket's own regression back into `add_comment` left
it green. Patchset 2 re-earned `LLM-Review +1` (clean PASS, no advisories) and `Verified +1` on
the strengthened oracle.

### Measured boundary: one mutation nothing kills

Stated as a boundary rather than left implicit. Mutating the SHARED helper
`outbound_comments.fit_preserving_marker` — shrinking its binary-searched prefix by 7 characters
— leaves this file green AND the wider comment suite green (`marker_survives_truncation`,
`length_convergence`, `richtext_port_heldout`: 18 passed under it). Nothing in the repo kills it.

I classify it an EQUIVALENT MUTANT, not a coverage hole: it violates no stated contract. The
body still carries its marker, still fits the budget, and both sides still agree — no assertion
anywhere requires the retained prefix to be MAXIMAL. Killing it would require introducing a
"fit as much as possible" contract, which is a widening rather than a bug fix, so it was
deliberately not added under a bug ticket.

Its converse is the design point: convergence genuinely IS preserved when the shared helper
changes, because both sides call it. That is what "share one fitter so they cannot drift" buys,
and it is why the send-path DRIFT mutation — not the in-helper one — is the mutation that had
to discriminate. It does.

### Attribution

`--caused-by=789c-1251-fc21-4cf6` (`emersed-specific-mutt`), `--class=regression`. Established
by re-running both transforms at that commit's parent (`32767 == 32767`, converged) versus
current main (`32767` vs `31753`, diverged), not by blame proximity — the originating commit is
not the file the fix lands in.

### Follow-on work filed (survives this ticket)

- `aragonite-bleached-vipersquid` (`17c3-2f6e-a5e0-438c`) — the rich-mode decode asymmetry that
  still blocks end-to-end equality under this project's `rich_text_cutover = "cloud"`. NOT fixed
  here; wider blast radius (it bites in-limit markdown comments too).
- `equivalent-unpacified-loris` (`4b87-e163-cd9e-43c8`) — the tautology class itself: convergence
  tests that re-derive the send path instead of driving it, with both instances from this area
  as worked examples.
